cargo_and_validation.goal: Reduce the dependency closure and feedback time for a small unit edit while retaining full production-boundary proof.

rules.text: Use the narrowest authoritative package/lib/test/feature target for the changed unit; compile/static success is not a runtime verdict.
Before costly work, use the current gameplan skill/controller and check the applicable moment; exact resource/candidate overrides remain scoped.
Build targets and proof artifacts stay in the governed external Handshake_Artifacts root with WP/MT/owner scope; no repo-local target.
Bind cache compatibility to source inputs, toolchain, target triple, features, profile and build configuration. Reuse compatible compiler artifacts without sharing mutable proof stores.
Serialize Cargo jobs that share a mutable target or disk/resource lane. Parallel teams do not authorize simultaneous Cargo use of one target.
Keep one chosen target warm for compatible work. Do not create a fresh target every retry, copy whole target trees, run cargo clean or retune the compiler/profile merely to start a phase.
Map changed inputs to dependent proof. Run focused checks first; broaden after the inputs stabilize and when authoritative acceptance requires it.
Run compatible proof selections as one union batch per package at a stable candidate while isolating every mutable DB/runtime fixture and retaining zero-match failure checks.
A changed source/config/binary invalidates dependent proof; unchanged evidence may be reused only if every relevant input and asserted behaviour remains unchanged.
Measure package rebuilds, relinked binaries and warm-check latency before claiming performance benefit; no RAM/CPU/SSD diagnosis or predicted speedup from crate count.
Preserve original timing assertions, features, timeouts and negative/error/rollback behaviours unless the Operator explicitly changes their contract.
